name: 5 Whys Root Cause Analysis
deliverable: Uncovered underlying structural failures rather than symptoms

steps.text: Write the symptom as a fact: what happened, when, how many, and for how long. Agree it first.
Ask why that state was possible, and record the direct enabling condition at each level.
Reject 'a person forgot' as a stopping point; ask what let one action run unchecked.
Keep one primary chain, noting plausible side branches in the margin instead of chasing them.
Stop when you reach a policy, gate, or architecture choice this team can actually change.

failure: The chain ends at a name or splits into competing trees, so the room leaves with blame or a diagram instead of a fix.
intervention: Say the person was the trigger, not the cause. Ask what safeguard was missing, and follow the one path that was necessary and sufficient.
provenance: Source protocol: the steps follow the written script in the source.

origin.note: Developed by Sakichi Toyoda and used at Toyota; no single canonical publication.
